title: The worker brief says how a filed bug is handed back, and sprint plan asks a rule-guarding item's open choices before start
goal: (a) The kb-sprint run brief (.claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md), .claude/agents/kb-worker.md and kb/_self/backlog.md say how a worker hands back a bug it filed with backlog.py new bug: it commits the new item file alone, in a commit of its own on work/<id> whose KB-Work names the new bug, and names the bug in its report, so no untracked item file is left to make land refuse the worktree; done's scope rule allows this, since kb/_self/backlog/** is always in scope (bl_base.ALWAYS_IN_SCOPE) and a commit of item files only is no work commit (bl_land.item_commits). (b) /kb-sprint plan lists, before the start gate is asked, each committed item whose touches are rule-guarding (the agents-rule paths of _tools/bl_authority.py) and asks each choice its goal leaves open as a blocking gate then, not after the code. Each rule is a tested question of kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv in the kb-worker and kb-sprint:plan sets. From the SP-hyp6o7hl retrospective.

run:
import re,subprocess as sp,sys
P=lambda *a:sp.run([sys.executable,'_tools/rag.py','pack','--root','_self',*a],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
Q=[('a sprint worker filed a bug with backlog.py new bug: how does its new item file reach the landing','kb-worker'),('before a sprint starts, which committed items get their open choices asked as blocking gates because their touches are rule-guarding','kb-sprint:plan')]
R=[]
for q,s in Q:
    m=re.search(r'coverage: good \(tested question (\S+):',P(q));R.append(bool(m) and ('# %s:'%m.group(1)) in P('--set',s));print(s,m.group(1) if m else 'no tested question',R[-1])
sys.exit(0 if all(R) else 1)

notes: Premise: python3 _tools/rag.py pack --root _self with each of the check's two questions shows coverage weak, no tested question, on 2026-10-06 (the check exits 1); in SP-hyp6o7hl a worker's new bug left an untracked item file in its worktree that blocked land, and BG-dudqrf5p (rule-guarding bl_authority touches, an exit-code choice its goal left open) got its gate after the code. kb-worker.md rule 5 already says to commit the filed bug's item file, but the kb-sprint run brief says only 'file a bug ... do not fix it' and kb/_self/backlog.md is silent on it. Why a rule-delivery check and not a text match: workers and planners read these rules through rag.py pack --root _self --set, so the check asks the questions a worker and a planner would ask and requires a tested question in their sets; the skill and agent text itself is not matched. Overlaps ST-zzsbdbi7 (same skill, agent and runbook files, another sprint): land one after the other.
